is frequently measured by ICP-MS, although AAS is a common alternative. Levels of copper in other tissues or ﬂuids are difﬁcult to
assess or are not considered valid indices of copper status.
Different copper functional tests are available: serum ceruloplasmin, erythrocyte superoxide dismutase (SOD), and leukocyte/
platelet cytochrome c oxidase assays. Serum ceruloplasmin can be measured for its oxidase activity on various substrates or by radial
immunodiffusion. The majority of serum copper is bound to ceruloplasmin, resulting in a similar response for these two markers.
